newsitem.title: INDIA: Delay in Bhopal relief cash angers Indian deputies.
newsitem.headline: Delay in Bhopal relief cash angers Indian deputies.

text.p: Indian parliamentarians, speaking on the 12th anniversary of the Bhopal gas tragedy which killed 6,500 people, on Tuesday criticised the government over delays in providing rehabilitation to survivors.
"Thousands of Bhopal residents died on this day in 1984 and hundreds of thousands were affected," said Suresh Pachauri, a lawmaker in the upper house of the parliament.
"No initiative has been taken on the proposed plan of 3.16 billion rupee of the Madhya Pradesh government for the years 1997 to 2000," Pachauri said.

In the world's worst industrial disaster, deadly gas leaked from a pesticides plant owned by a unit of U.S.-based Union Carbide Corp at Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh state. Some 6,500 people were killed and at least 20,000 were injured.
"What concrete action has the government taken for the last 12 years? What steps is it taking now?" asked Ashok Mitra, of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) CPI(M).
Several members of the upper house (Rajya Sabha) urged the government to submit a status report on the steps taken to rehabilitate the Bhopal gas victims.

"I will ask the minister concerned to give a complete report on the steps taken to rehabilitate Bhopal gas victims and (say) where the lapses are," the United News of India quoted Najma Heptulla, deputy chairman of the Upper House as saying.
"We have to think twice before inviting foreign direct investment into areas which are important and not into areas which are least important," said Y. Radhakrishna Murthy of CPI(M).
